knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.4.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines the moment generating function and cumulant generating function?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the MGF and CGF definitions.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The MGF is an exponential expectation and the CGF is its logarithm. A few moments are not the full function.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: M(t)=E[e^{tX}]; K(t)=log M(t), where the MGF exists.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating a stated mean and variance as though they were the MGF.

choices.label: Where it exists around t=0, M_X(t)=E[e^{tX}] and the cumulant generating function is K_X(t)=log M_X(t). Knowing only a mean and variance does not determine that the MGF has been obtained.
M_X(t)=E[tX] and K_X(t)=e^{M_X(t)}, so both are linear in t.
An MGF is simply the pair (E[X],Var(X)); no function of t is required.
Every random variable has a finite MGF for every real t, so existence conditions never matter.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.4.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. If X is Poisson with parameter λ, which MGF and CGF pair is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Summing E[e^{tX}] under the Poisson PMF gives exp(λ(e^t-1)); taking its logarithm gives the CGF.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Replacing the generating function with the mean and variance or swapping MGF and CGF.

choices.label: M_X(t)=exp(λt) and K_X(t)=λt because the mean alone determines the full Poisson MGF.
M_X(t)=λ(e^t-1) and K_X(t)=exp(λ(e^t-1)), so the MGF and CGF are reversed.
M_X(t)=λ and K_X(t)=log λ because Poisson mean and variance both equal λ.
